SERVED(1) - General Commands Manual

# NAME

**served** - manage personal services on Linux and macOS

# SYNOPSIS

**served**\
**served**
**edit**
\[**-f**&nbsp;*file*]
\[**-e**&nbsp;*editor*&nbsp;|&nbsp;**-&#45;path**]\
**served**
**enable**
\[**-f**&nbsp;*file*]
\[**-&#45;workdir**&nbsp;*directory*]\
**served**
**run**
\[*options*]
**-**&zwnj;**-**
*program*&nbsp;\[*arguments&nbsp;...*]\
**served**
**start**&nbsp;|&nbsp;**stop**&nbsp;|&nbsp;**disable**&nbsp;|&nbsp;**restart**&nbsp;|&nbsp;**attach**
\[*name*]\
**served**
**history**
\[*name*]
\[**-&#45;run**&nbsp;*id*]
\[**-e**&nbsp;*editor*&nbsp;|&nbsp;**-&#45;path**&nbsp;|&nbsp;**-&#45;stdout**&nbsp;|&nbsp;**-&#45;json**]\
**served**

**served**
**daemon**
\[**-&#45;handoff**&nbsp;|&nbsp;**-&#45;relinquish**]\
**served**
**shutdown**

# DESCRIPTION

**served**
runs commands from prepared projects as per-user services.
It does not upload code, install project dependencies, or build projects.
Linux and macOS are supported.
Run without a subcommand to open the service management TUI.
A manager must already be running for service management commands;
**edit**
works without a manager.

Service names are unique across enabled and temporary services.
Multiple services may share a working directory.
Lifecycle and history commands with no name match the current working directory.
If several services match, the command fails and lists names to choose from.
Named commands work from any directory.

# COMMANDS

**edit**

> Open the selected configuration in an external editor.
> **-f**, **-&#45;file** *file*
> selects any filename; otherwise discover the default configuration in the current directory.
> Create a commented JSON5 template when no configuration exists.
> Explicit file selection also creates missing parent directories.
> Existing text, including invalid configuration, is preserved. **-&#45;path**
> creates a missing template and prints its absolute path without opening an editor.
> Warnings go to standard error.
> **-e**, **-&#45;editor** *command*
> selects the editor and conflicts with **-&#45;path**.

**enable**

> Load configuration, register an enabled service, and start it.
> **-f**, **-&#45;file** *file*
> selects an explicit JSON5 file without filename discovery or deprecation warnings.
> A missing or invalid explicit file is an error; no fallback occurs. **-&#45;workdir** *directory*
> sets a persistent working directory override.
> Without an explicit file, discover configuration in this directory, or in the current directory
> if no working directory was specified.
> The effective directory must exist.
> See
> [served(5)](config.md)
> for resolution and registration details.

**run**

> Create and start a temporary service from the arguments after
> **-**&zwnj;**-**.
> Arguments retain their original boundaries; use an explicit
> **sh** **-c**
> for shell syntax.
> This command ignores all project configuration and dotenv files.
> It prints the service name after successful creation.
> Temporary services support the same management commands as enabled services.
> They survive manager handoff and crash recovery while their runner remains alive.
> Normal manager shutdown removes them; they do not restart after a host reboot.

**disable**

> Stop the named service and remove its enable record or temporary runtime definition.
> Persistent logs remain available on disk.

**start**

> Start a stopped or failed managed service.
> Do not register an unknown service.
> A running, starting, or automatically restarting service is unchanged, without reloading configuration.
> For a stopped enabled service, reload and validate its registered source before starting.
> Invalid configuration leaves it stopped.
> Temporary services reuse their original definition and environment.

**stop**

> Stop the service process and cancel automatic restarts, even with restart=always.
> Keep its registration, runner, and log history.
> An already stopped service is unchanged.
> Close active attach sessions; history remains readable.
> Manual stop survives handoff, relinquish, and manager crash recovery while the runner is alive.
> A live manager also preserves a known manual stop when replacing a failed runner.
> If both are lost, there is no durable stop flag.
> Normal shutdown followed by a fresh manager start, or a host reboot, starts enabled services again;
> temporary services are not restored.

**restart**

> Validate and reload an enabled service from its registered source before stopping its old process.
> An invalid configuration or directory leaves the old process running.
> Temporary services reuse their original launch definition.
> Renaming an enabled service requires disable, configuration edit, and enable.
> Restart also starts a stopped service.
> There is no separate service-level reload command.

> Start and stop require a runner with support for these operations.
> An older runner retained during an upgrade returns an error and is left unchanged.
> Disable it, then enable again with its original configuration source and working directory override,
> or run the temporary service again with its original arguments and environment.
> This recreation discards in-memory history; persistent logs remain.

**attach**

> Connect directly without opening the management TUI.
> PTY services allow one interactive writer; pipe services allow multiple read-only observers.
> Show a short sanitized snapshot, then relay live output.
> Ctrl-C detaches and is not forwarded to the service.
> A terminal is needed for interactive attach; use history output in automation.

**history**

> Read the latest run by default, or select an archived run with **-&#45;run** *id*. **-&#45;stdout**
> prints sanitized text; **-&#45;json**
> prints sanitized text and metadata as JSON.
> These modes also support memory-only history. **-&#45;path**
> prints the raw log path for a persisted run.
> Without an output mode, open the persisted raw log in an editor.
> **-e**, **-&#45;editor** *command*
> chooses that editor.
> Editor, path, stdout, and JSON modes are mutually exclusive.
> Raw paths and editor mode are unavailable for memory-only runs.

**list**

> Print managed services, their kind, state, PID, TTY mode, restart policy, and effective directory.
> A listed service may have exited; inspect its state and history.

**daemon**

> Run the manager in the foreground under a process supervisor.
> The official installers integrate with systemd on Linux and launchd on macOS. **-&#45;handoff**
> replaces the running manager with the requesting executable while preserving runners. **-&#45;relinquish**
> asks the manager to exit with status 75 while preserving runners for another supervisor.
> These options are mutually exclusive.

**shutdown**

> Stop the manager and all managed runners.
> Enabled registrations remain for the next manager start; temporary definitions are removed.

# OPTIONS

**-h**, **-&#45;help**
prints help for the selected command.
**-V**, **-&#45;version**
prints the executable version when used without a subcommand.

# RUN OPTIONS

**-&#45;name** *name*

> Service name; defaults to a sanitized form of the final working directory name.

**-&#45;workdir** *directory*

> Process working directory; defaults to the invocation directory.

**-&#45;no-tty**

> Use pipes instead of the default PTY.

**-&#45;no-sync-rows-cols**

> Keep the initial PTY size instead of following the attach client's terminal size.

**-&#45;restart** *policy*

> One of never, on-failure, or always.
> Default: never.

**-&#45;persist-logs**

> Persist raw output on disk.
> Default: memory-only output.

**-&#45;log-max-bytes** *bytes*

> Maximum size of a persistent log segment.
> Default: 10485760; must be positive.

**-&#45;log-max-files** *count*

> Number of archived persistent segments.
> Default: 3; must be positive.

**-&#45;env** *KEY=VALUE*

> Override one manager environment value with a literal value.
> Repeat for multiple values; the last duplicate key wins.

# TUI CONTROLS

Use Up/Down or j/k to select a service, s to start, x to stop, r to restart, d to disable,
a to attach, and h to browse history.
Enter opens the action menu; ? opens contextual help.
Disable requires confirmation and defaults to Cancel.
Use q or Escape to leave a view.
The borderless layout requires at least 40 columns and 10 rows.
Long service details can be read on the actions page with PageUp/PageDown.
While the manager is unavailable, the list is marked stale and service actions are blocked.
Success messages clear after three seconds; errors remain until dismissed.
In history, Enter opens a run; PageUp/PageDown and Home/End navigate its content.
The TUI does not edit service configuration.

# ENVIRONMENT

`HOME`

> Determines configuration and state paths for this user.
> XDG\_CONFIG\_HOME, XDG\_STATE\_HOME, and XDG\_RUNTIME\_DIR do not override these paths.

`EDITOR`

> Editor fallback after a command-line editor.
> Otherwise search PATH for editor, sensible-editor, nvim, vim, vi, nano, micro, then hx.
> Editor commands may contain arguments; the file path is appended as the last argument.

`RUST_LOG`

> Controls diagnostic logging.

# EXIT STATUS

Zero indicates command success, not that the service will remain running.
Errors return a nonzero status.
Editor failures propagate their status.
A manager intentionally relinquishing control exits with status 75.

# EXAMPLES

	served edit -f /configs/api.json5
	served enable -f /configs/api.json5 --workdir /srv/api
	served run --name worker --workdir /srv/api -- ./worker
	served list
	served history api --json
	served restart api
	served disable worker
